items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: I remember near the — earlier in the spring of 1980 I was working with Jim Ring and Phil Pearle and Peter Millet in the Physics Department.

ctx.x: Did you have thoughts about, okay, post-Hamilton what am I going to do in music?

I kind of knew by end that I wanted to be going into the recording aspect, the production aspect of music. I had, on campus I had the campus band for my junior and senior year called Rogue, and we were playing all the house parties and doing that. And we had started to write some original stuff. And I had actually stayed up here a year after I graduated. I graduated in ’79 so I stayed up one further year. We were trying to see if we could keep the band together and do something with it. And that kind of didn’t…

So I put in an application and they called me up and said, “oh we’d love to have you” and I was awarded a full fellowship for studying solid state physics at Columbia.
